transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! I'm feeling okay, thanks for asking. I do have a few questions about my recovery. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start with light exercise, including gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, make sure to be gentle and avoid any heavy lifting or bending. It's also a good idea to wear protective eyewear when gardening. Is there anything else you'd like to know about your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as was prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. And if you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma, or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, that’s good to know. I'm also finding that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild, just wearing sunglasses when you're going outside might help. But if it's severe or you're also experiencing pain and redness, we may need to assess it further. Would you like to know more about what to expect with your eyesight in the first few weeks after surgery?

transcript.text: Okay, that’s reassuring to hear. I don't have any more questions at the moment. Thanks so much for your help!
